messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: AUTH-SIGN-FAIL (critical) — Spike in JWT verification failures across multiple services. Link: https://pd.company/rely/INC-8421

pagerduty: Triggered by service: auth-verifier-prod. Urgency: high. Escalation policy: primary oncall (emma).

emma: Acked. I'm on it — moving convo to #incidents. @raj @maria @oliver please join.

raj: Joining. seeing tons of 401s and these errors in verifier logs: `jwt::verify: invalid signature, kid=abc123, expected=def456`

maria: Any deploys to key-manager or token-issuer in last few hours? Could be a key rotation.

oliver: Token-issuer had a deploy ~3h ago (release 2026-03-14T10:12Z, sha: b7c9e3f). No direct key-manager deploys in last 24h from infra checks. Checking ALB/health.

emma: If issuer rotated signing key but jwks endpoint unavailable, verifiers would see new kid but fail to fetch keys -> invalid signature. Raj can auth-verifier accept multiple keys (fallback)? If not, we may need to rollback token-issuer.

raj: auth-verifier supports multiple kids in jwks cache. Config stored at `/etc/auth-verifier/jwks_cache.json`. It polls https://key-manager.internal/.well-known/jwks.json every 60s. But I'm seeing JWKS fetch failures:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 503
ERROR key-fetch: failed to fetch jwks: 503
```

oliver: ALB for key-manager shows 504s and backend instance CPU close to 100%. Cloudwatch: 10 minute spike correlated with the token-issuer deployment window. Possible backend pool exhaustion during rollout.

incident-bot: Paging secondary oncall (zach) in 120s if no progress.

zach: ACK. Scaling key-manager ASG from 6 -> 12. Also adding temporary capacity for jwks endpoint.

raj: I can push a quick hotfix to auth-verifier to add the previous kid into the jwks_cache and restart pods gradually so they accept both old/new keys. Will do a rolling restart of 2 pods first.

emma: Good. Maria, please prep status update for customers (impact summary). Oliver coordinate infra scaling.

maria: On it. Initial impact: ~35% of auth-protected API requests returning 401s globally, affecting token refresh and SSO flows. CS has a canned message ready. ETA for public status update: 12 minutes.

oliver: Scaling done. Key-manager instances healthy after scaling, ALB 5xx rate dropping. Suspect that a new config in key-manager changed JWKS path or temporarily returned 503 during rollout and coincided with token-issuer rotating keys.

raj: Hotfix applied to 2 pods. Logs show verifiers now accepting both kids; 401 rate dropping: 35% -> 8% in last 3 minutes. Rolling the rest (remaining pods) now.

emma: Good progress. Keep rolling and monitor traces for edge cases (long-lived cached tokens).

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: Incident acknowledged by emma; escalation paused.

zach: Completed full rolling restart of auth-verifier replicas with fallback jwks config. No errors on health checks. 200 responses for JWKS fetch confirmed.

maria: Posted initial status: "We are experiencing authentication failures for some customers due to a key verification issue; mitigations in progress." CS updated.

raj: After full rollout, auth error rate is ~1.2% (within normal variance). Verified by sampling logs and synthetic checks hitting multiple regions.

oliver: Confirmed key-manager now stable and serving JWKS correctly. Reverted temporary autoscale to baseline. ALB 5xxs alleviated.

emma: Root cause hypothesis: token-issuer rotated signing key during a window when key-manager returned 503s (due to a redeploy-induced overload), causing verifiers to observe a new `kid` but be unable to fetch the corresponding public key. This resulted in invalid signature errors and widespread 401s.

maria: Customer impact summary draft: - Scope: 35% of requests experienced auth failures at peak (all regions) - Services affected: API gateways, SSO/token refresh - Duration: ~12 minutes to mitigation, full recovery observed by +26 minutes - Mitigation: accept both old/new signing keys, scale key-manager, roll out stable key-manager image. ETA for final postmortem: 48 hours.

emma: Action items assigned:
- Raj: backfill hotfix into mainline repo, add automated fallback for jwks cache (ETA 48h)
- Oliver: harden key-manager deployment (graceful draining, circuit breaker) and add more aggressive ALB autoscaling during deploys (ETA 72h)
- Maria: publish incident status updates and coordinate customer comms (ETA 2h)
- SRE/Product: schedule postmortem review (owner: emma)

zach: I'll take overnight watch — handing off active pager to zach. Emma will be back tomorrow for the postmortem.

emma: Handing off to zach for overnight. If any regression, page me and escalate to maria and oliver.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation applied and service returned to normal. Incident closed by emma.

maria: Final note added to status page and Jira ticket INC-8421 created for follow-ups. Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC.

raj: Logs/artefacts saved to s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-14/auth-sign-fail/ for the postmortem.

oliver: Adding monitoring alert tweaks to avoid paging for short JWKS fetch blips (follow-up PR).

emma: Thanks team. Great runbook execution — we'll capture learnings in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
